background.speaker: SPEAKER_00
background.text: So pivoting slightly to something that is dear to many people's hearts and yours as well as the mother of two kids under six, school reopenings. The republicans bill does include some funding for for schools which is something that you've said is necessary. ground_truth: Well, first and foremost, I want to thank all the educators out there because as someone who's been trying to homeschool a five-year-old, let me just tell you, I am not trained to do this. And like most moms, I desperately want my daughter to be able to go back and have a regular classroom experience and get the training, the teaching that she gets from a trained educator. That said, I also don't want her to contract COVID-19 and be sick or bring that illness home into the household where I have a 79-year-old mom who lives with me and a two-and-a-half-year-old baby as well. So the bill that the Republicans are proposing has some money for schools, not enough money, but that money is tied to you must reopen schools and bring students back. background.text: So just to return to a little aside there, I think some people might be surprised that a sitting senator is actually homeschooling her own daughter right now. How is that going?

ground_truth: Well, four months ago, almost five months ago when this started, I had wonderful plans. We're going to do basic phonics. At this point, five months later, it's like, here, kiddo, five worksheets. You get those done. You're done. It's so difficult. It's so difficult, and it is humbling. You know, I have a Ph.D., and I'm a U.S. senator, and I can fly helicopters, but I am not trained or equipped to teach a single five-year-old, and so I have nothing but abscess. I have no admiration for educators who do this voluntarily on a regular basis. God bless our teachers out there, and they need all the support that they can get to do the very difficult job that they're doing, and I see where I'm failing my daughter, and, you know, the mom guilt kicks in. The mom guilt kicks in because I see, like, oh, my gosh, she's not reading as well as she was when she was in the classroom, when she was on track, and now, you know, she doesn't know the difference between the p sound and the b sound, between a P and a B, and it's mom. It's my fault. I'm the one that's letting her down, and she's going to be behind the other kids when school comes back to normal. You know, all that mom guilt piles on top of everything. So it's hard for working families out there.
